metadata.title: One Prompt. Every Time.
metadata.purpose: Teach viewers what a Claude Skill is, walk them through the four steps to install and use Ruben's /how-to skill, and show them why Skills are the upgrade from prompting to having a permanent playbook.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

props.command: What is: One Prompt. Every Time?

beats.narration_text: Olá. This is Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude: how do I stop rewriting the same instructions every time I open a chat? Here's what that looks like — and it comes down to one concept called Skills.

props.ask: How do I stop rewriting the same instructions every time I open a chat?
props.answer_preview: Save them once as a Skill. Trigger with /slash command…
props.command: Someone asked Claude: how do I stop rewriting the same instructions every time I open a chat?

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a pre-made prompt that teaches Claude how to do something specific — without you having to repeat yourself. You save it once. Then you activate it with a slash command: type the slash, the skill name, and one line about your task. Claude loads the full instructions and gets to work. Anything you have explained to Claude twice should already be a Skill.

card.sub: /skill-name + one line. Claude loads your full playbook.

beats.new_visual_element: [SPARK] what a Skill is — save-once concept card

beats.narration_text: Four steps to install and use the /how-to Skill from Ruben's newsletter. Step one: download the skill file from the Dropbox link in the newsletter — it's free. Step two: go to Claude, open Settings, find Skills under Capabilities, click the plus, and upload the file. Step three: test it — open a new chat, type /how-to, add whatever you want to do with Claude but don't know how. Step four: use it in Cowork with Opus 4.8 on High effort for the best results.

illustration.concept: Four-step horizontal flow diagram on cream. Step 1: download cloud icon with label 'Download skill'. Step 2: upload arrow into settings icon labeled 'Upload to Skills'. Step 3: chat bubble with '/how-to' typed in, labeled 'Test it'. Step 4: Cowork tab icon with model selector, labeled 'Use in Cowork + Opus 4.8'. Terracotta accent on step numbers only. Connecting arrows between each step.
illustration.layout: Left-to-right horizontal flow, four equal boxes with connecting arrows, step numbers in terracotta circles above each box

beats.new_visual_element: [ILLUSTRATION] four-step Skill install and use flow

beats.narration_text: Skills travel. They work in Claude Chat, Claude Cowork, Claude Code — and according to the author, they also carry into ChatGPT and Gemini, because a skill is just a prompt file. Your playbooks move with you regardless of which AI you open.

card.sub: Author's claim: the same skill file works in Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini.

beats.narration_text: The sharpest way to run a Skill is inside a Project with Opus 4.8 on High effort. The Skill carries your how — your method, your voice, your rules. The Project carries your what — the client context, the files, the history. Opus 4.8 on High provides the intelligence to execute both well. That combination is where the outputs stop feeling generic.

card.sub: Skill = how. Project = what. Opus 4.8 = the intelligence to run it.

beats.new_visual_element: [SPARK] Skill plus Project plus Opus stack card

beats.narration_text: Building your own Skill is simple. Option one: use the built-in /skill-creator — Claude interviews you and writes the skill for you. Option two: go to makemyskill.com — a free tool Ruben built for exactly this. Option three: if you're already in a good chat session with Claude, just ask it to make the conversation into a skill. Your library grows one skill at a time.

illustration.concept: Three-path diagram showing three routes to building a Skill. Path A: a chat bubble labeled '/skill-creator' with a Claude logo. Path B: a browser window labeled 'makemyskill.com'. Path C: a chat history icon with an arrow labeled 'make this a skill'. All three paths converge to a single skill file icon with a lightning bolt. Terracotta on the converging arrow only.
illustration.layout: Three parallel paths from left, merging into a single output on the right, hand-drawn on cream

beats.new_visual_element: [ILLUSTRATION] three ways to build a Skill diagram

beats.narration_text: This week: think of one thing you keep explaining to Claude over and over — a writing style, a research format, a type of analysis. Download Ruben's /how-to skill from the newsletter link, install it in three clicks, and run it once. Then immediately create your own first skill from whatever you explained today. Two installs, one session.

card.sub: Download /how-to. Run it once. Then build your own first skill from today's chat.

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. One Prompt. Every Time. Stop retyping. Start building the library that works for you.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you want to build a Claude skill — a reusable prompt that produces the same type of output every time you need it. Ask Claude to show you the skill anatomy: the three elements that make a prompt reusable rather than one-off, how to test the skill against edge cases, and where to store it so it's available every session.

props.command: I want to build a Claude skill — a reusable prompt that produces the same type of output every time I need it. Show me the skill anatomy: the three elements that make a prompt reusable rather than one-off, how to test the skill against edge cases before relying on it, and where to store it so it's available in every session without re-pasting.
Take what you learned from [One Prompt. Every Time.] and apply it to your own work. What's one thing you'll try first?
